title: The wall broken down (Ephesians 2:11–22)
hook: Christ is our peace, breaking the dividing wall
tomorrow: kneel or stand to pray? the Bible has both. which is right?

segments.voice: Yesterday: his workmanship, people made on purpose, for good works. Today Paul looks at something people built between themselves.

Some walls you can lean on. Others you can't see at all: who sits where, whose wedding you're invited to, which side of town you grew up on. Paul writes that Christ "hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us." Here's the strange part. He never says which wall. No street, no stones, no name. Just the middle wall, as if his readers would know. So which one was it?
screen: `WALLS YOU CAN'T SEE.` → `THE MIDDLE WALL OF PARTITION.` → `WHICH WALL?`

segments.voice: Some readers think of a real one: a low stone barrier in the Jerusalem Temple, which the historian Josephus says warned foreigners not to go further. The letter itself never names it. What Paul does name is the two peoples on either side. He reminds Gentile believers they were once "far off," outside the promises God made to Israel, and now "are made nigh." Then: "For he is our peace, who hath made both one." Both: Jewish and Gentile believers. Notice Paul doesn't call Christ a peacemaker who negotiates a truce. He says Christ is the peace. And the wall doesn't get a door cut in it, so one side can visit on certain days. It comes down. Then the purpose: "for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace." Here's one to tell a friend: the Greek word behind man there is the everyday word for a human being. One new humanity, made out of two. Then Paul trades walls for a house: "ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God." Not guests. Family. Jewish readers understand God's covenant with Israel on their own terms, and this letter speaks of peace made in Christ. Which wall was it? Paul cares less about the stones than about what goes up in their place.
screen: `A TEMPLE BARRIER? THE LETTER DOESN'T SAY.` · `FAR OFF, MADE NIGH.` · `ONE NEW HUMANITY, OUT OF TWO.` · `FELLOWCITIZENS, THE HOUSEHOLD OF GOD.` · then, large: `HE IS OUR PEACE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person a quiet wall has gone up with, built from a misunderstanding or just from time. Write them a short, plain text with no argument in it: thinking of you, or I miss our talks. Hold it through the sit, and send it if it still feels right.
The wall broken down. Paul's picture of Christ removing the barrier between two peoples, and building one household.
The line to keep: he is our peace, not a truce but a person. Take care.

fork.setup: a friend says Paul's 'middle wall' was definitely a specific stone wall in the Temple. what's the fair answer?
options: some readers think so, but the letter itself never names one.
yes; Paul names the Temple wall in the very next verse.

fork.reveal: some readers connect it to a Temple barrier that Josephus describes. the letter names only what the wall kept apart: two peoples, now made both one.

chat.meaning: He is our peace, who hath made both one… of twain one new man. Not one side winning: something new built from both.

Temple.meaning: the house of God in Jerusalem, at the center of Jewish worship

Josephus.meaning: a Jewish historian who wrote in Roman times

Puzzle: the letter does not name the 'middle wall'. 'Some readers' connect it to the Temple balustrade that Josephus says warned foreigners not to pass (Jewish War 5.193–194; Antiquities 15.417). The lesson keeps the hedge and gives no date. Confirm.
New fact: the Greek behind 'one new man' (2:15) is ἄνθρωπος, the ordinary word for a human being; the lesson says 'one new humanity'. Confirm the wording.

Framing: the lesson presents Israel's covenants as the promises the Gentile readers were far from, adds that Jewish readers understand God's covenant with Israel on their own terms, and does not unpack 2:15's 'law of commandments contained in ordinances', which churches and Jewish readers read in different ways. Confirm that Judaism is not cast as the foil.
'Christ is the peace itself, not a peacemaker' is a reading of 'he is our peace'; confirm.

Unity thread (owner's 'one human race'): the 'one new humanity' fact is stated as what the Greek word is, not as a claim that all religions are one; the passage is about Jewish and Gentile believers in Christ.
